introduction:
A Registered Will is a pivotal legal instrument that ensures your assets and properties are distributed precisely according to your final wishes. By formally registering the Will under the Indian Registration Act, 1908, you provide it with an undisputed legal backing, significantly minimizing the chances of future familial disputes or fraudulent claims in Delhi.

Registration ensures the document is safely preserved in the official government custody (Book No. 3), providing an authentic reference that cannot be easily tampered with, destroyed, or forged.
quickFacts:
Important to Know
  • Mandatory: No, registering a Will is optional but highly recommended for legal authenticity.
  • Jurisdiction: Under the "Anywhere Registration Policy" in Delhi, you can register your Will at any Sub-Registrar’s office in Delhi, though choosing one near your residence is most convenient.
  • Government Fees: ₹600 total (₹500 Registration Fee + ₹100 Pasting Charge).
  • Stamp Duty: ₹0 (No stamp duty is required for a Will).
  • Time Taken: Usually completed in 1 visit (approx. 1–2 hours) if the appointment is booked.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required for Will Registration

Note: Prepare one original set and one set of photocopies.
For the Testator
  • The Will: The original Will printed on plain A4 paper (legal ledger paper is also fine), signed by the Testator and two witnesses.
  • ID Proof: Aadhaar Card, Passport, Voter ID, or PAN Card.
  • Address Proof: Aadhaar Card, Driving License, or Utility Bill.
  • Photographs: Two passport-sized color photos.
  • Medical Certificate (Optional but Recommended): If the Testator is elderly (70+), a doctor’s certificate confirming "sound mind" is strongly advised to prevent future legal challenges.
For the Two Witnesses
  • Required Documentation: Must have their own original ID and Address Proofs (Aadhaar/PAN) along with two passport-sized color photos of each witness.
  • Note: Witnesses can be family members, but it is legally safer if they are not beneficiaries in the Will to avoid conflicts of interest.
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Online Appointment Booking

Important: Delhi requires you to book an appointment online before visiting the office.
Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Step 1: Visit Portal: Visit the Delhi Revenue Department official website (revenue.delhi.gov.in) or the e-District Delhi portal (edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in).
  2. Step 2: Access Appointment Section: Look for the "Appointment Management System" or "e-Registration" section.
  3. Step 3: Register/Login: Register/Login using your mobile number.
  4. Step 4: Select Service: Select "Registration of Deeds" -> "Will".
  5. Step 5: Enter Details: Enter the basic details of the Testator and the area/jurisdiction to see available slots.
  6. Step 6: Choose Slot: Choose a Sub-Registrar office (SRO) and a convenient date/time.
  7. Step 7: Print Confirmation: Download and print the Appointment Acknowledgement Slip.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Physical Visit (Offline Process)

Note: The registration is physically completed at the Sub-Registrar's Office (SRO) on the day of your booked appointment.
Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Step 1: Arrive Early: Arrive at the chosen SRO at least 15 minutes before your slot.
  2. Step 2: Get Token: Go to the reception or "Facilitation Counter" and show your Appointment Slip to get a token number.
  3. Step 3: Appearance: When your number is called, the Testator and both witnesses must appear before the Sub-Registrar.
  4. Step 4: Document Verification: The official will verify your documents and IDs.
  5. Step 5: Biometrics: The officer will take digital photos and fingerprints of the Testator and witnesses.
  6. Step 6: Fee Payment: You will pay the ₹600 fee at the counter (cash or demand draft is typically accepted, but carry cards/UPI just in case).
  7. Step 7: Sign Register: You will sign the register in the presence of the officer.
afterApplying:
After Will Registration - Next Steps

Collect Receipt

You will be given a receipt/acknowledgment slip after the registration process is done at the SRO.

Collection Timeline

The registered Will is scanned and stored. In most digital SROs in Delhi, you get the original hard copy back on the same day or the next working day.

Storage & Safekeeping

The government keeps a digital copy. You should keep your original Registered Will in a safe place (e.g., a bank locker).
